newsitem.title: INDIA: India gets ninth consecutive normal monsoon rains.
newsitem.headline: India gets ninth consecutive normal monsoon rains.

text.p: India had the ninth consecutive normal monsoon in 1996 (July-September) with 32 of 35 pockets receiving normal to excess rains, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Monday.

"For the country as a whole, the total rainfall during the monsoon season was 102 percent of its long period average value, making 1996 the ninth successive normal monsoon," IMD said in its end-of-season report.
It said 83 percent of the country's districts received normal to excess rains. "This year's rainfall distribution is better than that for the last five years and is comparable to that of 1990."
The report said only three pockets of western Vidarbha, eastern Orissa and northeastern states of Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura had marginally deficient rains.
It said the monsoon was in its withdrawal phase.
"As on October 7, the southwest monsoon has withdrawn from greater parts of north India. It is likely to withdraw from the remaining parts of the country during the next fortnight," the IMD said.

Monsoon rains hit southern Kerala state on June 3, two days later than normal but covered the entire country by June 30, two weeks earlier than normal. The onset of the monsoon was characterised by two tropical cyclones, one over the Bay of Bengal and another over the Arabian sea.
